# Roof rack strut channel installation

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Remove fender bolt and double a webbing strap to create loops for installation. [t271]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove the fender bolt located near the front of the vehicle.
2. Double a 12-inch length of webbing strap over itself to create a loop.
3. Heat one end of a steel bolt with a blowtorch until red hot.
4. Push the heated bolt through both layers of the doubled strap to melt holes at each end.
5. Insert the fender bolt back into its hole and thread it through the webbing loops on either side.
6. [Partial] Tighten the bolts down securely.

_Procedure reported by [t271]._

## Tools

- Pliers [t271]
- Blowtorch [t271]

## Parts

- 12-inch lengths of good quality webbing strap, pair [t271]
- Steel bolt or suitable steel item for heating [t271]

## Specifications

- **Webbing length per side**: 12 inches [t271] ([Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Use solid (not slotted) unistrut channels for easier reconfiguration of spring nut locations. [t271]
- [Partial] Snip springs shorter with a diagonal cutter and bend the end back to fit low-profile strut channels. [t271]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Cranking down too hard on the strap ends, which can break surrounding parts or tear fabric edges. [t271]
